1	# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim
2	
3	Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
4	`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
5	(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
6	measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
7	target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
8	in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.
9	
10	How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
11	component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
12	initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
13	emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
14	The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
15	NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
16	exactly the current ROI envelope.
17	
18	Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
19	- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
20	  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
21	- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
22	  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
23	  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
24	- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
25	  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
26	- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
27	  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
28	  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
29	  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
30	  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
31	  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.
32	
33	Verified facts this design stands on (probed 2026-07-15)
34	- HTIF window file I/O works on QEMU + all 3 vsim engines, 26 MB/s,
35	  1984 B/chunk; `_gettimeofday` works.
36	- C++ exceptions/ctors work bare-metal; printf INSIDE the ROI works on
37	  the vsim leg; a 3.6 MB image crossing the DLM window (0x200000)
38	  survives the handoff bit-exact.
39	- Hybrid QEMU leg is engine-synced (`-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), no
40	  zfh/zvfh; RTL is ELEN=32. llama.cpp must be built with
41	  `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF -mext-zvlsseg`.
42	- Standalone fast mode pins `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` (Zce, no Zcd): FP code
43	  from the default multilib traps there. vlinux runs are engine-synced
44	  or must pass `-- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` until U2 fixes the
45	  default for `--runtime linux`.
46	- Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf is architecture `qwen3` (2560 embed, 36 layers,
47	  32 heads, 32768 ctx, 398 tensors) - a standard llama.cpp arch, no
48	  custom model code needed. Confirmed end-to-end OUTSIDE andesim
49	  (2026-07-15): `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/run-rv64-qemu.sh` runs the
50	  cross-compiled `llama-completion` under Andes's linux-user QEMU
51	  (`qemu-riscv64`, syscall translation, no system emulation - a
52	  functional-only sanity check, unrelated to andesim's hybrid pipeline)
53	  and it generates correct text at `-t 1` ("The capital of France is
54	  Paris."), proving the model loads and every ggml op it needs already
55	  runs on RVV. That build (`build-rv64/`, `build-rv64-noomp/`) is
56	  **dynamic** (`BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`) with `GGML_RV_ZFH/ZVFH/CPU_REPACK=ON`
57	  - the opposite link mode and feature set vlinux needs (static,
58	  those three OFF per the line above), so U8 still needs its own build;
59	  this only de-risks the syscall/threading/model-format assumptions.
60	- `build-rv64-baremetal/` (a prior newlib-baremetal attempt via
61	  `cmake/riscv64-andes-elf-newlib-gcc.cmake`) is abandoned: the
62	  toolchain file no longer exists and it produced zero binaries. Not a
63	  usable shortcut around vlinux; ignore that directory.
64	
65	## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)
66	
67	| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
68	|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
69	| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
70	| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
71	| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |
72	| vlinux                  | 0x0200_0000 .. 0x0220_0000     | proxy text/data/bss + its own stack (2 MB) |
73	| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
74	| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
75	| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |
76	
77	DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
78	across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
79	Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly
80	(no silent vplat-style `_sbrk` corruption).

268	  like tests/andes_sim/*)
269	- Depends on: U6, U7

271	
272	## U9. Hybrid: one-kernel-iteration ROI
273	
274	- Description: the actual goal. Two supported ways to delimit ONE
275	  iteration: (a) marker build - a 5-line llama.cpp patch snippet
276	  (documented, kept in docs/) adds `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers around the
277	  target op guarded by an iteration counter (`if (++n == K)`), markers
278	  are HINT NOPs so the same binary still runs everywhere; (b) no-source
279	  route - `andesim profile` finds the hot loop, then `--trigger pc
280	  --pc-start/--pc-end` with symbols resolved from the app ELF (U2).
281	  Results print INSIDE the ROI (nothing after ROI-end executes - the
282	  existing contract). Expectation note for the guide: one Bonsai-4B-shape
283	  (2560 embed) q1_0 matvec is smaller than the original 27B estimate
284	  (~10-100 M cycles there) -> likely faster than minutes-to-~1h at
285	  vsim's 9-50 kHz, confirm actual figure once measured; a full token
286	  would still be far too slow - that is why we measure one iteration.
287	- Input/Output: hybrid run of a marker'd glibc matvec fixture (and then
288	  llama-completion with the counter patch) prints in-ROI checksum +
289	  `[andesim] N cycles`, N stable across two runs (deterministic single hart).
290	- Key files: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/llama_roi_howto.md (new, with the
291	  counter-marker snippet), tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_hybrid_roi.sh
292	- Depends on: U4 (fixture), U8 (llama-completion variant)
293	- State: PLANNED
294	
295	## U10. Platform track: DRAM window >= 6 GB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]
296	
297	- Description: lift the 2 GiB ceiling so the untouched 3.8 GB GGUF +
298	  arenas (~4.5 GB) fit. Three coordinated changes: (1) qemu_andesim

306	  First step is a spike: confirm the RTL decode location and cost; if

308	- Input/Output: `--mem-size 6G` accepted; U8 smoke passes with the full

310	- Key files: qemu_andesim (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c), hybrid_vsim repo,

312	- Depends on: independent of U0-U9 (parallel track). NOT needed for the
313	  primary Bonsai-4B goal (fits 2 GiB directly) - only for a 27B revisit.
314	- State: PLANNED

316	## U11. Bridge tool: GGUF layer-slice script (host side) [stretch, off critical path]
317	
318	- Description: `scripts/gguf_slice.py` (gguf-py): keep the first K
319	  transformer blocks + embeddings + output head, rewrite
320	  `block_count`/tensor list, so Bonsai-27B becomes a <= 1.5 GB model
321	  whose per-layer kernel SHAPES are identical to the real one. This is
322	  the U8/U9 workload until U10 lands. Sliced-model quality is garbage
323	  (fine - we measure kernels, not perplexity).
324	- Input/Output: `python scripts/gguf_slice.py Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf 12`
325	  -> `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.k12.gguf`, loads in stock llama.cpp on the host,
326	  `llama-completion` runs on it.
327	- Key files: scripts/gguf_slice.py (new)

330	  goal - only for a 27B revisit (see U10).

332	
333	---
334	
335	Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first - every feature's contract
336	above is a grep-able stdout/exit-code check, so its RED test goes in

# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim

Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.

How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
exactly the current ROI envelope.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.

Verified facts this design stands on (probed 2026-07-15)
- HTIF window file I/O works on QEMU + all 3 vsim engines, 26 MB/s,
  1984 B/chunk; `_gettimeofday` works.
- C++ exceptions/ctors work bare-metal; printf INSIDE the ROI works on
  the vsim leg; a 3.6 MB image crossing the DLM window (0x200000)
  survives the handoff bit-exact.
- Hybrid QEMU leg is engine-synced (`-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), no
  zfh/zvfh; RTL is ELEN=32. llama.cpp must be built with
  `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF -mext-zvlsseg`.
- Standalone fast mode pins `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` (Zce, no Zcd): FP code
  from the default multilib traps there. vlinux runs are engine-synced
  or must pass `-- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` until U2 fixes the
  default for `--runtime linux`.
- Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf is architecture `qwen3` (2560 embed, 36 layers,
  32 heads, 32768 ctx, 398 tensors) - a standard llama.cpp arch, no
  custom model code needed. Confirmed end-to-end OUTSIDE andesim
  (2026-07-15): `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/run-rv64-qemu.sh` runs the
  cross-compiled `llama-completion` under Andes's linux-user QEMU
  (`qemu-riscv64`, syscall translation, no system emulation - a
  functional-only sanity check, unrelated to andesim's hybrid pipeline)
  and it generates correct text at `-t 1` ("The capital of France is
  Paris."), proving the model loads and every ggml op it needs already
  runs on RVV. That build (`build-rv64/`, `build-rv64-noomp/`) is
  **dynamic** (`BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`) with `GGML_RV_ZFH/ZVFH/CPU_REPACK=ON`
  - the opposite link mode and feature set vlinux needs (static,
  those three OFF per the line above), so U8 still needs its own build;
  this only de-risks the syscall/threading/model-format assumptions.
- `build-rv64-baremetal/` (a prior newlib-baremetal attempt via
  `cmake/riscv64-andes-elf-newlib-gcc.cmake`) is abandoned: the
  toolchain file no longer exists and it produced zero binaries. Not a
  usable shortcut around vlinux; ignore that directory.

## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)

| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |
| vlinux                  | 0x0200_0000 .. 0x0220_0000     | proxy text/data/bss + its own stack (2 MB) |
| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |

DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly
(no silent vplat-style `_sbrk` corruption).

---

## U0. Extract shared HTIF window client (structural)

- Description: move the window protocol client (`win_syscall`, slot
  staging, chunk loop) and `uart_putc` out of `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
  into `runtime/htif_client.{c,h}` so vplat and vlinux share one
  implementation. No behavior change.
- Input/Output: existing vplat fixtures before == after.
- Key files: runtime/htif_client.c (new), runtime/htif_client.h (new),
  runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, runtime/Makefile
- Test: existing tests/vplat/*.sh all stay green (that IS the test).
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - htif_uart_putc/htif_syscall/htif_win_*/
  htif_call_str*/htif_write/htif_read now live in runtime/htif_client.{c,h};
  vplat_syscalls.c is a thin newlib adapter over them. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh green before and after (byte-identical output).

## U1. vlinux skeleton: boot, banner, manifest reader

- Description: new `runtime/linux/` payload with its own crt.S + linker
  script at 0x0200_0000 (built with HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, freestanding +
  newlib for internal printf). Boots via `-bios vlinux.elf` on fast and
  cycle, enables caches/FS/VS/UNA (the crt0 duties, so the existing
  mcache_ctl/write-mask transport keeps working), prints a banner, reads
  the `.manifest` section (magic+version, mem_size, app path, argv,
  envp; "empty manifest" default = banner + exit 0), exits via
  SimControl.
- Input/Output: `vlinux.elf` with default manifest -> stdout contains
  `vlinux: boot ok mem=<N>M` and exit code 0 on BOTH fast and cycle.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{crt.S,vlinux.ld,main.c,manifest.h},
  runtime/linux/Makefile, scripts/build_all.sh
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh (fast leg + sim_ax45mpv_premium)
- Depends on: U0
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{manifest.h,main.c,vlinux.ld,
  Makefile} + tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh + scripts/build_all.sh
  `vlinux` target. No new crt.S: ../crt0.S (shared with vplat) enables
  icache/dcache/mstatus.FS+VS/mmisc_ctl.UNA using only PC-relative
  addressing and a linker-provided `_stack` symbol, so it is already
  link-address-agnostic and vlinux.ld's `PROVIDE(_stack = 0x02200000)` +
  `. = 0x02000000` base retarget it with zero new code (CLAUDE.md: don't
  duplicate code). vlinux.elf links main.c straight against
  build/runtime/{crt0.o,libandesim_runtime.a} (no -specs=andesim.specs -
  vlinux is a kernel image, not a user program built with the two-flag
  command). Confirmed via research (QEMU andes_ae350.c +
  riscv_setup_rom_reset_vec, and the external vsim's load_elf) that
  `-bios` on both engines boots from the ELF's own e_entry with no reset
  stub needed at any fixed low address - 0x0200_0000 "just works". Test
  runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag yet -
  that's U2): `./andesim run --mode fast` + `sim_ax45mpv_premium` direct,
  same pattern as tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh + f2.sh. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh + the build_all.sh/release_surface driver contract
  tests stay green.

## U2. Driver: `--runtime linux` plumbing

- Description: new run flag. The driver copies vlinux.elf per run and
  `objcopy --update-section .manifest=<blob>` (toolchain objcopy from
  config.env) with: absolute app ELF path, `mem_size`, argv[0..n] (from
  `-- <args...>`, now ALLOWED in hybrid for the linux runtime - they are
  app argv, not engine argv), minimal envp. The manifested vlinux.elf is
  what every leg loads, so fast/cycle/hybrid stay uniform. Linux runtime
  defaults: `--mem-size 1G`; standalone fast leg uses the engine-synced
  CPU (`andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), not the ax46 default. `--pc-start/end`
  symbols resolve against the APP ELF in this mode.
- Input/Output: `./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf -- -m x.gguf -t 1`
  -> dry-run prints the objcopy step + `-bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf`;
  manifest blob round-trips (dump tool or readelf grep).
- Key files: driver/cli.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/manifest.cpp (new), docs/USER_GUIDE.md
- Test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh (dry-run
  contract + manifest content grep)
- Depends on: U1
- State: PLANNED

## U3. ELF loader + Linux initial stack + auxv

- Description: vlinux HTIF-reads the app ELF (26 MB/s -> ~0.5 s for a
  10 MB binary), maps PT_LOADs (reject overlap with vlinux/V-scratch/
  window), zeroes BSS tails, builds the initial stack at the top of the
  app arena: argc/argv/envp then auxv (AT_PHDR/PHENT/PHNUM from the
  loaded headers, AT_ENTRY, AT_PAGESZ=4096, AT_RANDOM 16 bytes,
  AT_HWCAP=IMAFDCV bits, AT_UID/GID/EUID/EGID=0, AT_SECURE=0,
  AT_EXECFN), sets sp, jumps to the app entry in M-mode.
- Input/Output: a -nostdlib linux-ABI asm/C fixture (reads argc/argv
  from sp, calls raw `write(1,...)` + `exit_group`) prints its argv and
  auxv AT_PAGESZ. Proves loader+stack with only 2 syscalls, before glibc.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{loader.c,stack.c}, tests/fixtures Makefile
  (new LINUX_TOOLCHAIN fixtures; config.env.example gains
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d)
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh (fast + cycle, argv echo)
- Depends on: U1, U2
- State: PLANNED

## U4. Syscall core: glibc reaches main()

- Description: M-mode ecall handler + dispatch table. Set 1 (the ones a
  static glibc needs from `_start` to `printf`+`malloc`+`exit`):
  exit(93), exit_group(94), write(64)/writev(66) fd1/2 -> UART,
  brk(214), mmap(222 MAP_ANONYMOUS)/munmap(215)/mprotect(226 noop),
  set_tid_address(96), set_robust_list(99), rseq(293 -ENOSYS),
  uname(160; release "6.1.0-andesim" - MUST be >= the binary's "for
  GNU/Linux 4.15.0" note or glibc aborts), getpid/gettid/getuid/geteuid/
  getgid/getegid (1/1/0/0/0/0), prlimit64(261), getrandom(278;
  rdcycle-seeded), sched_getaffinity(123; 1-cpu mask), sched_yield(124),
  rt_sigaction(134)/rt_sigprocmask(135)/sigaltstack(132) -> record+0
  (no delivery exists), tgkill(131) on fatal signal -> SimControl exit
  128+sig, ioctl(29 -ENOTTY), fcntl(25 basic). Unknown syscall -> print
  `vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once + return -ENOSYS (loud, grep-able).
- Input/Output: glibc-static fixture using argv + malloc(1MB) + printf +
  fflush + exit(42) -> exact stdout + exit code 42, fast AND cycle.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{trap.S,syscall.c,mm.c}
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh
- Risk to check here: Andes vendor glibc may use riscv_hwprobe(258) for
  str* ifuncs at startup -> implement as -ENOSYS first (glibc falls back
  to generic); if the vendor libc hard-requires it, answer the base
  key set instead.
- Depends on: U3
- State: PLANNED

## U5. File I/O syscall set (HTIF window bridge)

- Description: openat(56), close(57), read(63), pread64(67), lseek(62),
  fstat(80), fstatat(79)/statx(291 basic mask), faccessat(48),
  readlinkat(78 -EINVAL), getcwd(17), getdents64(61 -ENOSYS). All
  bridge to the existing window ops (open/read/lseek/fstat already
  host-served); paths are host-side, same semantics as vplat file I/O.
  stdin read -> 0 (EOF), as today.
- Input/Output: glibc fixture fopen/fread/fseek/ftell-checksums a host
  file; byte-identical result fast vs cycle (parity, like vplat_file).
- Key files: runtime/linux/syscall.c, runtime/htif_client.h
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh
- Depends on: U4
- State: PLANNED

## U6. Time syscalls

- Description: clock_gettime(113) for REALTIME + MONOTONIC (both from
  the window GETTIMEOFDAY host clock; MONOTONIC = delta from a boot
  baseline so it never goes backward), clock_getres(114),
  nanosleep(101)/clock_nanosleep(115) -> return 0 immediately (no timer
  exists; sleeping burns no sim time). This makes `ggml_time_us()` work
  unpatched. Note: values are HOST wall time - meaningful on the fast
  leg, meaningless inside a vsim ROI (the cycle figure is the answer
  there).
- Input/Output: glibc fixture prints two monotonic stamps with
  delta >= 0 around a 10M-loop; llama-style timing pattern compiles and
  runs.
- Key files: runtime/linux/syscall.c
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_time.sh
- Depends on: U4
- State: PLANNED

## U7. File-backed private mmap (llama.cpp default load path)

- Description: mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE, PROT_READ...) = allocate from the
  mmap arena + HTIF-read the range (private read-only copy is
  semantically correct for GGUF loading). Region table for munmap /
  partial unmap (llama unmaps unused tail ranges); mremap -> -ENOMEM.
  Arena exhaustion -> -ENOMEM (llama then reports the real reason
  instead of corrupting). With this, stock llama.cpp default
  `use_mmap=true` works; `--no-mmap` also works via U5 read path.
- Input/Output: glibc fixture mmaps a 64 MB host file, checksums,
  munmaps; same checksum as host `sha256sum` prefix.
- Key files: runtime/linux/mm.c
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_mmap.sh
- Depends on: U5
- State: PLANNED

## U8. llama.cpp acceptance on the fast leg

- Description: document + script the static build and prove end-to-end
  text generation. Build recipe (docs/USER_GUIDE.md new section):
  riscv64-linux-gcc/g++, `-static`, `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`,
  `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON` is fine now (glibc has everything),
  `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`, `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF
  GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`, `-mext-zvlsseg`, `GGML_NATIVE=OFF` - a fresh
  static build; the existing `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/build-rv64*`
  dirs are dynamic and wrong-feature-set for this (see verified facts),
  not reusable as-is. Run: `./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux
  llama-completion -- -m Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -t 1`.
- Input/Output: generated completion text printed to stdout, exit 0,
  with `--mem-size` sized to the 572 MB model + 300 MB headroom (1G
  covers it, same default U2 sets).
- Key files: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh
  (env-gated: needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN + Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf; manual-tier
  like tests/andes_sim/*)
- Depends on: U6, U7
- State: PLANNED

## U9. Hybrid: one-kernel-iteration ROI

- Description: the actual goal. Two supported ways to delimit ONE
  iteration: (a) marker build - a 5-line llama.cpp patch snippet
  (documented, kept in docs/) adds `<andesim/ROI.h>` markers around the
  target op guarded by an iteration counter (`if (++n == K)`), markers
  are HINT NOPs so the same binary still runs everywhere; (b) no-source
  route - `andesim profile` finds the hot loop, then `--trigger pc
  --pc-start/--pc-end` with symbols resolved from the app ELF (U2).
  Results print INSIDE the ROI (nothing after ROI-end executes - the
  existing contract). Expectation note for the guide: one Bonsai-4B-shape
  (2560 embed) q1_0 matvec is smaller than the original 27B estimate
  (~10-100 M cycles there) -> likely faster than minutes-to-~1h at
  vsim's 9-50 kHz, confirm actual figure once measured; a full token
  would still be far too slow - that is why we measure one iteration.
- Input/Output: hybrid run of a marker'd glibc matvec fixture (and then
  llama-completion with the counter patch) prints in-ROI checksum +
  `[andesim] N cycles`, N stable across two runs (deterministic single hart).
- Key files: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/llama_roi_howto.md (new, with the
  counter-marker snippet), tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_hybrid_roi.sh
- Depends on: U4 (fixture), U8 (llama-completion variant)
- State: PLANNED

## U10. Platform track: DRAM window >= 6 GB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]

- Description: lift the 2 GiB ceiling so the untouched 3.8 GB GGUF +
  arenas (~4.5 GB) fit. Three coordinated changes: (1) qemu_andesim
  andes_ae350 machine model DRAM window (currently "Cannot model more
  than 2GB RAM"); (2) vsim RTL platform address decode for the same
  window (external hybrid_vsim/RTL config - needs its own
  investigation: is the testbench memory size parameterizable per
  engine build?); (3) driver `max_program_mem_bytes()` (driver/
  shm.cpp:91), memmap print, and the vlinux arena bounds (already
  mem_size-driven). ABI is u64 addresses throughout - no wire change.
  First step is a spike: confirm the RTL decode location and cost; if
  the RTL cannot grow, evaluate a high-DRAM alias window instead.
- Input/Output: `--mem-size 6G` accepted; U8 smoke passes with the full
  Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf resident; U9 measures its layer-0 kernel.
- Key files: qemu_andesim (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c), hybrid_vsim repo,
  driver/shm.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, docs/USER_GUIDE.md
- Depends on: independent of U0-U9 (parallel track). NOT needed for the
  primary Bonsai-4B goal (fits 2 GiB directly) - only for a 27B revisit.
- State: PLANNED

## U11. Bridge tool: GGUF layer-slice script (host side) [stretch, off critical path]

- Description: `scripts/gguf_slice.py` (gguf-py): keep the first K
  transformer blocks + embeddings + output head, rewrite
  `block_count`/tensor list, so Bonsai-27B becomes a <= 1.5 GB model
  whose per-layer kernel SHAPES are identical to the real one. This is
  the U8/U9 workload until U10 lands. Sliced-model quality is garbage
  (fine - we measure kernels, not perplexity).
- Input/Output: `python scripts/gguf_slice.py Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf 12`
  -> `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.k12.gguf`, loads in stock llama.cpp on the host,
  `llama-completion` runs on it.
- Key files: scripts/gguf_slice.py (new)
- Test: host-side pytest-style check of tensor count + metadata.
- Depends on: nothing (host tool). NOT needed for the primary Bonsai-4B
  goal - only for a 27B revisit (see U10).
- State: PLANNED

---

Rollout: one feature per session, TDD-first - every feature's contract
above is a grep-able stdout/exit-code check, so its RED test goes in
tests/vlinux/ (or tests/andes_sim/ for U2) before the implementation.
Update docs/USER_GUIDE.md as each lands.

Order: U0 -> U1 -> U2 -> U3 -> U4 -> U5 -> {U6, U7} -> U8 -> U9. That is
the full path to the primary goal (llama-completion + Bonsai-4B,
fast leg then hybrid ROI). U10 and U11 are an optional 27B stretch
track, off the critical path entirely (U11 any time; U10 is the only
cross-repo item) - only worth picking up if/when Bonsai-27B specifically
is requested.

Compound effect: U0-U7 give andesim a general "run Linux userspace
binaries" capability - every future glibc workload (SPEC kernels,
libnn perf tests, any vendor benchmark) reuses vlinux with zero
per-app porting, and U9's counter-marker recipe becomes the standard
way to cycle-measure ONE iteration of any hot kernel inside a large
application. When FR-109 (real Linux, S/U+paging) eventually lands,
its acceptance workloads and test fixtures are already here.

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
42	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
43	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
44	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
45	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
46	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
47	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
48	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
49	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
50	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
51	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
52	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
53	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
54	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
55	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
56	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
57	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
58	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
59	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
60	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
61	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
62	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
63	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
64	};
65	
66	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
67	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
68	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
69	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
70	
71	}  // namespace andes_sim
72	
73	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
74

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- there is no QEMU2 handback leg.
2	// run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	  // The QEMU CPU model the fast leg must instantiate ({qemu_cpu} fill),
34	  // parsed from the same probe's `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` globals: the
35	  // readconfig globals only apply to THAT driver, and a mismatched model
36	  // silently ignores them (found live: andes-ax45mpv kept vlen=512 when the
37	  // ax66 run asked for 128). Empty => the family default (andes-ax45mpv).
38	  std::string qemu_cpu;
39	};
40	
41	// The family-default QEMU CPU model: the -cpu fallback when an engine's
42	// --print-qemu-config names none. One definition, used by the plan executor's
43	// {qemu_cpu} fill and by cmd_profile's engine-synced launch.
44	inline constexpr const char* kDefaultQemuCpu = "andes-ax45mpv";
45	
46	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
47	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
48	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
49	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
50	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
51	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
52	}
53	
54	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
55	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
56	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
57	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
58	// themselves).
59	struct LegTriggerArgs {
60	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
61	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
62	};
63	
64	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
65	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
66	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
67	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
68	//
69	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
70	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
71	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
72	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
73	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
74	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
75	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
76	                                std::string& err);
77	
78	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
79	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
80	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
81	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
82	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
83	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
84	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
85	
86	// The QEMU CPU model named by a `--print-qemu-config` probe's text: the first
87	// `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, stripped of the "-riscv-cpu" suffix.
88	// "" when the text names none (probe failed / engine without the hook) -- the
89	// caller falls back to the family-default -cpu.
90	std::string qemu_cpu_from_cfg(const std::string& cfg_text);
91	
92	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
93	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
94	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
95	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
96	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
97	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
98	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
99	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
100	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
101	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
102	
103	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
104	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
105	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
106	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
107	
108	struct PlanOptions {
109	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
110	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
111	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
112	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing
113	};
114	
115	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
116	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
117	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
118	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
119	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
120	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
121	                               int got_rc);
122	
123	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
124	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
125	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
126	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
127	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
128	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
129	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
130	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
131	
132	}  // namespace andes_sim
133	
134	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
135

1	// argv assembly for `run --mode fast|cycle`.
2	//
3	// The framework parses only its selection flags; everything after `--` is the
4	// engine's own CLI. passthrough_argv fills the engine's role invoke template
5	// ({bin}/{elf}) and appends those verbatim args. cmd_run then runs the result
6	// either transparently (exec_passthrough -- fast: inherited stdio, an
7	// interactive gdbstub / monitor / console unchanged) or filtered
8	// (run_cycle_clean -- cycle: hide the banner + [info], restate the cycle count).
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PASSTHROUGH_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PASSTHROUGH_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	
17	namespace andes_sim {
18	
19	// Assemble the argv: fill `eng`'s `role` invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) then
20	// append `passthrough` verbatim. On an unknown role or unknown placeholder,
21	// sets `err` and returns {}. `elf` is substituted as-is; validating that a
22	// positional was actually given is the caller's job.
23	std::vector<std::string> passthrough_argv(
24	    const EngineDescriptor& eng, const std::string& role, const std::string& elf,
25	    const std::vector<std::string>& passthrough, std::string& err);
26	
27	}  // namespace andes_sim
28

1	// The three models andesim composes from engines. A model says *which*
2	// engines run and *how* they combine; the concrete engine(s) are resolved
3	// separately (built-in qemu, or a discovered verilator:<cfg>).
4	//
5	//   fast      = QEMU alone (functional), transparent passthrough.
6	//   cycle     = one Verilator alone, pure from reset, transparent passthrough.
7	//   hybrid    = QEMU fast-forwards, Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_MODELS_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_MODELS_HPP
10	
11	#include <string_view>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	struct Model {
16	  std::string_view name;
17	  std::string_view engines;  // engine composition, for `list models`
18	  std::string_view notes;
19	};
20	
21	inline constexpr Model kModels[] = {
22	    {"fast", "qemu64 | qemu32", "functional"},
23	    {"cycle", "vsim:<cfg>", "cycle-accurate"},
24	    {"hybrid", "qemu64 -> vsim",
25	     "QEMU fast-forwards, vsim measures the ROI; "
26	     "pick --trigger marker|pc"},
27	};
28	
29	inline const Model* find_model(std::string_view name) {
30	  for (const Model& m : kModels)
31	    if (m.name == name) return &m;
32	  return nullptr;
33	}
34	
35	}  // namespace andes_sim
36	
37	#endif  // ANDESIM_MODELS_HPP
38

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	  // The engine whose hardware the fast leg(s) must model when the plan has
50	  // NO accurate-leg step of its own (the --verify oracle plan): the ISA sync
51	  // ({vlen}, {qemu_cpu}, -readconfig, LM sidecars) reads this engine instead.
52	  // Empty => derive from the plan's accurate-leg step (the normal case).
53	  std::string hw_engine_id;
54	};
55	
56	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
57	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
58	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
59	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
60	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
61	struct PhaseResult {
62	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
63	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
64	  std::string out;
65	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
66	};
67	
68	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
69	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
70	struct PlanResult {
71	  std::string error;
72	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
73	  // The concrete per-step argv run_plan built (after placeholder fill, qemu_cfg
74	  // staging, and state threading). Populated whether or not the steps spawn, so
75	  // a --dry-run can print the exact commands without executing them.
76	  std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> argvs;
77	  // On a leg failure: where the kept evidence lives (the workdir's drain/
78	  // sidecar/cfg files, a copy of the ELF, manifest.txt). Empty on success or
79	  // when the bundle could not be written.
80	  std::string repro_dir;
81	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
82	};
83	
84	}  // namespace andes_sim
85	
86	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
87

1	// The pure core of `run --mode hybrid`: turn the CLI selection into a Trigger.
2	//
3	// Split out from cmd_run.cpp so it is unit-testable without spawning qemu/vsim.
4	// pc-mode boundaries are resolved against the ELF .symtab here (via elf_syms),
5	// so the live path in cmd_run only has to build the 2-step plan and run it.
6	#ifndef ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
7	#define ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
8	
9	#include <string>
10	#include <vector>
11	
12	#include "cli.hpp"
13	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
14	#include "plan.hpp"
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Build the ROI Trigger for a hybrid run from `cli` + `elf` (the ELF is needed
19	// to resolve pc-mode symbol boundaries). The pc boundaries are stored as
20	// "0x"-prefixed hex in params (enter_pc/exit_pc). On a missing/unresolvable pc
21	// boundary or unknown trigger, returns a Trigger with empty kind and sets `err`.
22	Trigger hybrid_trigger(const Cli& cli, const std::string& elf, std::string& err);
23	
24	// Build the vsim accurate-leg's user-forwarded extra args (verbatim tokens
25	// appended after the trigger args): kanata ROI visualization
26	// (`--kanata <f> --kanata-roi [--objdump <f>]`). `kind` is the trigger kind,
27	// used to validate: --kanata is marker/pc only; --objdump requires --kanata.
28	// On a violation returns {} and sets `err`. Absent kanata yields an empty
29	// list (the common case). Post-`--` args are NOT forwarded here -- hybrid
30	// rejects them up front (cmd_run), as the handoff owns both legs' argv.
31	std::vector<std::string> vsim_extra_args(const Cli& cli, const std::string& kind,
32	                                         std::string& err);
33	
34	// ISA-sync guard for the accurate-leg engine: the hybrid fast leg is a 64-bit
35	// QEMU, so an engine reporting xlen != 64 cannot share architectural state
36	// with it. Returns "" when the pairing is valid, else the diagnostic. An
37	// engine that reports no xlen (0) is accepted as-is.
38	std::string hybrid_hw_check(const EngineDescriptor& acc);
39	
40	}  // namespace andes_sim
41	
42	#endif  // ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
43

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
46	long long physical_mmap_bytes(long long program_bytes);
47	
48	// The largest --mem-size whose physical mmap still fits the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM
49	// window (program_bytes + scratch page <= 2 GiB). --mem-size is capped here.
50	long long max_program_mem_bytes();
51	
52	// First-fit resolver over `tiers`. `probe(dir)` returns the dir's free bytes,
53	// or -1 when it does not exist. A tier fits when probe >= size + margin.
54	// On success `err` is empty; when nothing fits, returns {"", ""} and `err`
55	// names every tier's reason plus the HSIM_MMAP_DIR hint. Pure: no env, no
56	// filesystem -- testable with a fake probe.
57	MmapDirChoice resolve_mmap_dir(
58	    const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers, long long size,
59	    const std::function<long long(const std::string&)>& probe,
60	    std::string& err);
61	
62	// The andesim cache root: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim, else ~/.cache/andesim,
63	// else "" (no HOME). Shared by the mmap tier list and the repro bundles.
64	std::string andesim_cache_dir();
65	
66	// Build the real tier list from the environment:
67	//   HSIM_MMAP_DIR set -> that single pinned tier;
68	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andesim
69	//                      (created here so the free-space probe can see it).
70	std::vector<MmapTier> mmap_tiers();
71	
72	// WSL2 advice for `doctor`: given /proc/version contents, the repo dir, and
73	// the mmap tier list, return warning lines. Empty when not on WSL2. On WSL2:
74	// always the .wslconfig memory= hint (tmpfs is capped by the WSL VM), plus a
75	// drvfs warning for the repo or any tier dir under /mnt/ (slow, and
76	// MAP_SHARED is not coherent across the 9p boundary). Pure -- testable.
77	std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,
78	                                      const std::string& repo_dir,
79	                                      const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers);
80	
81	// Convert a --mem-size spec into the fast leg's plain QEMU `-m` argv:
82	// {"-m", "<MiB>M"}. Empty spec -> {} with no error (QEMU as-is). Malformed
83	// specs and sizes that are not a whole MiB (QEMU's -m granularity) return {}
84	// and set `err`.
85	std::vector<std::string> qemu_m_args(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
86	
87	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the resolved dir (mkstemp +
88	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line
89	// (plus "; fallback: <why>" when /dev/shm was skipped), and return its path.
90	// On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file (unlink when
91	// done).
92	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
93	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
94	
95	}  // namespace andes_sim
96	
97	#endif  // ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
98

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46	
47	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
48	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
49	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
54

1	// Subprocess helpers for andesim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// is redirected to /dev/null; stderr too, unless relay_stderr is set, in
26	// which case the child inherits OUR stderr and its diagnostics stream live
27	// (used to surface the legs' leveled logs at --log-level <= debug). If the
28	// child runs longer than timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
29	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms,
30	                      bool relay_stderr = false);
31	
32	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
33	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
34	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
35	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
36	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
37	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
38	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
39	
40	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
41	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
42	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
43	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
44	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
45	
46	// Run argv with BOTH stdout and stderr captured (separate pipes) and stdin
47	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
48	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
49	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
50	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
51	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
52	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
53	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
54	int run_line_filtered(
55	    const std::vector<std::string>& argv,
56	    const std::function<void(int stream, std::string_view line)>& on_line);
57	
58	}  // namespace andes_sim
59	
60	#endif  // ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
61

# --dry-run applies to ALL run modes (fast, cycle, hybrid): it prints the exact
# command(s) andesim WOULD spawn, shell-quoted, and executes nothing. Regression
# guard for the bug where fast/cycle silently ignored --dry-run and ran the
# program (e.g. `run --mode fast hello.elf --dry-run` printed "hello").
#
# Layers:
#   1. fast   (always; needs only build/andesim + a fixture ELF): prints the
#      full qemu command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   2. cycle  (needs a built vsim engine; SKIPs otherwise): the vsim standalone
#      command, exit 0, executes nothing.
#   3. hybrid (regression): still prints 2 commands.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command and runs nothing. Use the
#    reported arg order (flag AFTER the ELF) to lock the repro.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-machine andes_ae350' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing the qemu command: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-bios' \
  || fail "fast --dry-run missing -bios <elf>: $out"
ok "fast: --dry-run prints the full qemu command, executes nothing"

# Resolve a built vsim engine the way the driver does (VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env) -- vsim_bin_dir comes from tests/lib/log.sh.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
SIM=$(ls "$BINDIR"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '\.(json|txt)$' | head -1)
if [ -z "$SIM" ] || [ ! -x "$SIM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP cycle + hybrid --dry-run: no built vsim engine under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi
id="vsim:$(basename "$SIM" | sed 's/^sim_//')"

# 2. cycle: standalone vsim engine, --dry-run previews its command, runs nothing.
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --dry-run \
      --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle --dry-run exit $rc (should preview, not run): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run did not print the preview banner (it executed?): $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "$(basename "$SIM")" \
  || fail "cycle --dry-run missing the vsim command: $out"

# 3. hybrid regression: still 2 commands (probe -> stage -> inject path intact).
out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
      --dry-run --engine "$id" "$elf" 2>&1)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the andesim runtime builds for BOTH arches from two
# toolchains. ARCH=rv64 (default) -> build/runtime/, ARCH=rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32/.
# The produced objects must be the right ELF class (rv64=ELFCLASS64, rv32=ELFCLASS32).
#
#   rv64 always runs (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32; SKIPs if unset.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val

elf_class() { od -An -j4 -N1 -tu1 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '; }   # 1=ELF32 2=ELF64

TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC64" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"

# rv64 (default ARCH): library + crt0 land in build/runtime and are ELFCLASS64.
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv64 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC64" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv64 runtime build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: missing build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/crt0.o")" = "2" ] \
  || fail "rv64 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS64"
ok "rv64 runtime -> build/runtime (ELFCLASS64)"

# rv32: needs the second toolchain. SKIP cleanly if absent.
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 runtime: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "rv32 runtime build failed (ARCH=rv32, HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$TC32)"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: missing build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ "$(elf_class "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/crt0.o")" = "1" ] \
  || fail "rv32 runtime: crt0.o is not ELFCLASS32"
ok "rv32 runtime -> build/runtime/rv32 (ELFCLASS32)"

1	// andesim leveled logging.
2	//
3	// The scale mirrors the vsim engines' --log-level option so users learn one
4	// scheme: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off. A message
5	// prints when its level >= the threshold; the default threshold is info.
6	//
7	// What lives at which level (driver policy):
8	//   info  -- the answers: program output relays, the cycle figure,
9	//            --dry-run/--verify results. Program output itself is never
10	//            gated (it is the program's, not a log).
11	//   debug -- driver chatter: the hybrid banner, the mmap line, PASS lines,
12	//            verify progress notes.
13	//   warn  -- degradations: unsupported-CSR warnings, skipped engines.
14	// Fatal errors are not gated: they accompany a non-zero exit.
15	#ifndef ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
16	#define ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
17	
18	#include <string>
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	enum LogLevel {
23	  kLogTrace = 0,
24	  kLogDebug = 1,
25	  kLogInfo = 2,
26	  kLogWarn = 3,
27	  kLogError = 4,
28	  kLogCritical = 5,
29	  kLogOff = 6,
30	};
31	
32	// Set the process-wide threshold from the CLI value. "" keeps the default
33	// (info). Returns false (and leaves the threshold alone) when the value is
34	// not an integer in 0..6.
35	bool set_log_threshold(const std::string& cli_value);
36	
37	// The current threshold (0..6). Used to forward the level to child engines.
38	int log_threshold();
39	
40	// True when a message at `level` should print.
41	bool log_on(int level);
42	
43	// Open the --log-file sink. Once open, EVERY log_line/log_result message --
44	// all levels, even below the console threshold -- is appended to the file
45	// with a UTC timestamp and a level tag. Returns false if the file cannot be
46	// opened (the sink stays off). Empty path is a no-op success.
47	bool set_log_file(const std::string& path);
48	
49	// The open sink's path, or "" when none.
50	const std::string& log_file_path();
51	
52	// Emit one chatter line to stderr when `level` passes the threshold. Pass
53	// the complete line text (including its "[andesim] " prefix), without the
54	// trailing newline. Always mirrored to the --log-file sink.
55	void log_line(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
56	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
57	
58	// Emit one RESULT line (the cycle figure, PASS/verify verdicts) to stdout
59	// when `level` passes the threshold. Always mirrored to the sink.
60	void log_result(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
61	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
62	
63	}  // namespace andes_sim
64	
65	#endif  // ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
66

## 5. The `run` options, one by one

Synopsis:

```
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
```

`run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
commands (`profile`, `list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.

### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)

Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.

### 5.2 `--engine <id>`

Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.

- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:

  ```
  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
  ```

Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
engine, up front:

```
andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
```

Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).

VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
wins):

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
```

The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  cmd_profile.cpp
  profile.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  log.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
  memmap.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp log.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp)
# hybrid guest memory-map composer (pure; descriptor + qemu.cfg text in, rows out).
add_executable(andesim-memmap-test memmap_test.cpp memmap.cpp)
# profile core: plugin-log/disasm parsing, RVV filter, loop nesting, renderers,
# QEMU argv builder (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-profile-test profile_test.cpp profile.cpp)

foreach(_t andesim-cli-test andesim-json-test andesim-infra-test andesim-plan-test andesim-plan-itest andesim-run-test andesim-vsimfilter-test andesim-elf-syms-test andesim-hybrid-test andesim-state-diff-test andesim-engine-registry-test andesim-memmap-test andesim-profile-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-state-diff-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# memmap reads HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (the reserved top page) from the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-memmap-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# hybrid-test reaches plan.hpp via hybrid.hpp; plan.hpp carries the drained
# record (hybrid_state_v1) since verify_oracle F4.
target_include_directories(andesim-hybrid-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U2 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
# linux app.elf -- <app argv>` stages a manifested vlinux.elf (this run's app
# path + mem-size stamped into its .manifest section via objcopy) and boots
# THAT under -bios, instead of the app ELF directly.
#
# Scope for U2: only --mode fast is wired (cycle/hybrid are rejected for now;
# hybrid wiring is ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9). App argv (-- ...) is accepted
# but not yet threaded into the manifest -- U3 adds the vlinux loader that
# consumes argv/envp -- so this run only proves the objcopy step + manifest
# app-path round-trip, matching the roadmap's Input/Output contract.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. dry-run contract: objcopy step printed, -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf,
#    engine-synced CPU, the 1G mem-size default, qemu itself stays a preview.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --dry-run "$elf" \
      -- -m x.gguf -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy' \
  || fail "missing the objcopy step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--update-section .manifest=' \
  || fail "missing --update-section .manifest=: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'dry-run: 1 command' \
  || fail "qemu itself should stay a preview (1 command), not run: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- '-bios [^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' \
  || fail "missing -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-m 1024M' \
  || fail "--runtime linux should default --mem-size to 1G: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
  || fail "missing the engine-synced CPU override: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'not wired yet' \
  || fail "should warn that app argv (-- ...) is not threaded through yet: $out"
ok "fast --runtime linux --dry-run: objcopy step + -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf"

# 2. manifest content round-trips: readelf -p on the staged ELF's .manifest

# F6 contract: `scripts/run_e2e.sh` works out of the box -- its default
# VSIM_BIN must be the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine
# (sim_ax45mpv_premium, the same default ./andesim pins), NOT the
# alphabetically-first VSIM_BIN_DIR sim_* (sim_ax45mpv_mp2, a 2-core
# config where crt0's secondary-hart SKIPPED write stops the sim before
# hart 0 drains and every C fixture fails).

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

### 5.11 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough

Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
`--mem-size`, ...) instead.

### 5.12 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel

Status: `--mode fast` only, for now (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` for the
full plan -- `cycle`/`hybrid` are rejected with a clear error until a later
feature wires them; `hybrid` is planned at U9).

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
```

The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.

Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.

Not there yet: your app's own argv/envp (`-- <args...>`) are accepted on the
command line (so the eventual `-- -m model.gguf -t 1` shape parses today) but
are NOT threaded into the app yet -- andesim prints a warning and drops them.
vlinux itself only boots and prints a banner so far; the ELF loader that
actually runs your app is a later feature. Track progress in
`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.

---
